---
title: "Introduction"
guide-section: "Getting Started"
---

tinytab is a small library for formatting values and rendering small tables, as text or as
HTML. It has no dependencies beyond Python itself.

It exists as an example: a small but complete package that shows how to structure, test, and
document a Python library. It isn't published on PyPI.

## Installation

Install tinytab from its GitHub repository:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
pip install git+https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package.git
```

## A first look

tinytab does three things. It formats single values as strings:

```{python}
from tinytab import fmt_currency

fmt_currency(1234.5)
```

It builds tables, with a formatter attached to any column:

```{python}
from tinytab import Table

menu = Table(
    {
        "item": ["coffee", "bagel", "croissant"],
        "price": [3.5, 2.25, 4.0],
    }
)

menu.fmt("price", fmt_currency)
```

And it summarizes sets of numbers:

```{python}
from tinytab import summarize

summarize([3.5, 2.25, 4.0])
```

The rest of this guide takes each of these in turn:

- [Formatting Values](formatting-values.qmd): numbers, percentages, and currencies
- [Tables](tables.qmd): building, formatting, rendering, and saving tables
- [Summary Statistics](summary-statistics.qmd): `summarize()` and its result object
